items.name: Theorem 1.2: tempered refinement of the Genestier–Lafforgue parameter of a discrete series
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over a local function field F of characteristic p and π an irreducible discrete series representation of G(F). There is a (necessarily unique) essentially tempered L-parameter L(π) : W_F × SL_2 → ^LG whose associated semisimple parameter, L^{ss}(π)(w) = L(π)(w, diag(|w|^{1/2}, |w|^{−1/2})) as in (1.1), is the Genestier–Lafforgue parameter L^{ss}(π).
items.note: Proved for essentially discrete series by Corollary 3.8 with Propositions 3.9 and 3.11.
items.proofState: unproved extraction target; open supplier obligations apply

items.name: Corollary 1.3: a tempered parametrisation refining Genestier–Lafforgue
items.statement: There is a well-defined map L : T(G(F)) → {essentially tempered L-parameters} refining the construction of Genestier–Lafforgue, where T(G(F)) is the set of classes of irreducible essentially tempered representations of G(F).
items.note: Tempered representations are reached from discrete series of Levi subgroups by parabolic induction, with which L^{ss} is compatible (Theorem 2.3(iv)). The paper notes that it does not show L(π) is elliptic for discrete series π.

items.name: Theorem 1.4(i): pure supercuspidal parameters are ramified
items.statement: Let F = k((t)) with k = F_q, q = p^m > 5, and G an unramified connected reductive group over F that is not a torus. Let π be an irreducible supercuspidal representation of the form π ≅ c-Ind_U^{G(F)} τ for a smooth irreducible representation τ, with Q̄_ℓ coefficients, of a compact open (modulo centre) subgroup U. If L^{ss}(π) is pure (for any Frobenius Frob_F, the eigenvalues of L^{ss}(π)(Frob_F) are Weil q-numbers of one weight), then L^{ss}(π) = L(π) is ramified: it is nontrivial on the inertia subgroup I_F.
items.note: The proof of the key step (Theorem 7.2) is incomplete when the k-simple factor of G is not absolutely simple (sourceIssues E1).
items.proofState: unproved extraction target; open supplier obligations apply

items.name: Theorem 1.4(ii): parameters of supercuspidals induced from sufficiently small subgroups are wildly ramified
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 1.4, if U is sufficiently small (Definition 8.2), then L^{ss}(π), and hence L(π), is wildly ramified: nontrivial on the wild inertia subgroup of W_F.

items.name: Theorem 1.5 = Theorem 7.12: pure unramified parameters come from unramified principal series
items.statement: Let F = k((t)) with |k| = q > 5 (a hypothesis the proof needs but the statement omits), G unramified reductive over F and σ an irreducible representation of G(F) whose Genestier–Lafforgue parameter L^{ss}(σ) is pure and unramified. Suppose every supercuspidal representation of every Levi factor of G(F) contains an 𝔰-type, as holds when p ∤ |W_G| (Fintzen) or p is odd and G is an unramified classical group (Stevens). Then σ is an irreducible constituent of an unramified principal series representation of G(F).

items.note: The proof applies Theorems 7.2 and 7.9 (or Corollary 7.11) to the supercuspidal support, which need q > 5; the statement omits it (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Theorem 2.1(i)–(ii): V. Lafforgue's global parametrisation and twisting
items.statement: (V. Lafforgue, Théorème 0.1) For a global function field K and connected reductive G over K there is a map L : A_0(G) → G^{ss}(G) from cuspidal automorphic representations with central character of finite order to classes of compatible families of semisimple ℓ-adic homomorphisms Gal(K^sep/K) → ^LG, such that at every place v with Π_v unramified, L(Π) is unramified at v and L^{ss}(Π)|_{W_{K_v}} is the Satake parameter of Π_v. For an algebraic character ν : G → G_m and a finite-order Hecke character χ, L(Π ⊗ χ∘ν) = L(Π)·ν̂∘χ̂.
items.note: GS.5 plans V. Lafforgue's excursion construction of global parameters with Satake compatibility (PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18 routes the source there). Printed 'For any Π ∈ 𝒢_0(G)' in (ii) (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Theorem 2.1(iii) and Theorem 2.3: the Genestier–Lafforgue local parametrisation
items.statement: (Genestier–Lafforgue, Théorème 0.1) For a place v and F = K_v, the semisimplification of L(Π)|_{W_{K_v}} depends only on F and Π_v; this extends to a semisimple parametrisation L^{ss} : A(G, F) → G^{ss}(G, F) of all irreducible admissible representations (2.2), which is (iv) compatible with parabolic induction: if π is a constituent of Ind_{P(F)}^{G(F)} σ, then L^{ss}(π) = i_M ∘ L^{ss}(σ); (v) for quasi-split G, if π^{I(p)} ≠ 0 for the pro-p radical I(p) of an Iwahori subgroup, L^{ss}(π) takes values in ^LT; (vi) compatible with homomorphisms Υ : G_1 → G_2 with normal image (in particular isogenies of semisimple groups): L^{ss}(π ∘ Υ) = ^LΥ ∘ L^{ss}(π), and likewise globally ([Laf18, Prop. 12.5]).
items.note: PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18 marked the Genestier–Lafforgue parametrisation and its local–global compatibility as planned in GS.7 (with GS.4); PAPER-FENG-24 routed its use through the Bernstein centre to its own Part II. For (vi) the restriction π ∘ Υ need not be irreducible; the statement is meant for its constituents.

items.name: Definition 2.5: purity relative to a specified faithful representation
items.statement: Fix a faithful algebraic representation τ of the finite-action L-group. A representation σ has a pure semisimple parameter relative to τ if, for every Frobenius lift, the eigenvalues of τ∘L^{ss}(σ) are Weil q-numbers of a single weight. This is a representation-relative predicate. The printed equivalence between some and every faithful τ is false (E15); the intrinsic central-weight convention needed by the main theorems is an open supplier, not silently defined by this predicate.
items.note: Do not change τ or identify this predicate with essential temperedness without a proved compatibility theorem.

items.name: Definition 3.1 and the Gross–Reeder dictionary: Weil–Deligne parameters and L-parameters
items.statement: Let C=ℂ, G be connected reductive over F, and use its dual group with the finite pinning-preserving Galois action. A Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameter is a continuous homomorphism ρ from W_F into the L-group, with the prescribed projection, open kernel on inertia and semisimple Frobenius, together with a nilpotent N in Lie(Ĝ) satisfying Ad(ρ(w))N=|w|N. For geometric Frobenius |Fr|=q^{-1}. Equivalence is by Ĝ-conjugation of both data.

items.name: Definition 3.2: tempered and essentially tempered parameters
items.statement: For the finite-action L-group and the complex analytic topology, a WD parameter is tempered if the Ĝ-coordinate of its associated φ(W_F×SU₂) is relatively compact. It is essentially tempered if its image after passage to Ĝ^{ad} and the finite action is relatively compact. The projection to Ĝ is used as a coordinate in the semidirect product, not asserted to be a homomorphism.

items.name: Definition 3.3(a): linear pure Weil–Deligne representations
items.statement: (a) A Weil–Deligne representation (ρ, N) on V is pure if there is t ∈ C such that (i) the eigenvalues of ρ_t(Frob_F) := ρ(Frob_F)q^t are q-numbers of integer weight; (ii) the subspace W_aV of (generalised) eigenvectors of ρ_t(Frob_F) with eigenvalues of weight ≤ a is (ρ, N)-stable; (iii) there is an integer w (the weight) with N^i : gr_{w+i}V → gr_{w−i}V an isomorphism for all i ≥ 0.

items.name: Lemma 3.6 (Sawin–Templier): local purity of irreducible global parameters
items.statement: (Sawin–Templier, [ST, Lemma 11.4]) Let X be a smooth projective curve over a finite field with K = k(X) and ρ : Gal(K^sep/K) → ^LG(C) irreducible (its image lies in no proper parabolic subgroup, parabolic subgroups defined dynamically via cocharacters λ : G_m → ^LG). For every place z, the Weil–Deligne parameter (ρ_z^{ss}, N_z) of the restriction ρ_z to a decomposition group at z is pure.
items.note: [ST] states it for split semisimple G; Remark 3.7 extends it to reductive G. The deduction uses the mixedness from L. Lafforgue and Weil II, Theorem 1.8.4 and Proposition 1.6.13.

items.name: Corollary 3.8: pure completions from irreducible globalisations
items.statement: Let π be an irreducible admissible representation of G(F). Suppose X is a smooth projective curve over a finite field, z a place of K = k(X) with K_z ≅ F, and Π a cuspidal automorphic representation of G_K with Π_z ≅ π whose global parameter L(Π) is irreducible. Then the Weil–Deligne parameter L_Π(π) = (L^{ss}(π), N_Π) of L(Π)|_{Γ_z} is pure, and it is the unique pure completion of L^{ss}(π).

items.name: Proposition 3.9: irreducible globalisations of supercuspidals
items.statement: Let π be a supercuspidal representation of G(F), X a smooth projective curve over a finite field and z a place of K = k(X) with K_z ≅ F. There are infinitely many cuspidal automorphic representations Π of G_K with Π_z ≅ π and L(Π) irreducible. In particular L^{ss}(π) has a pure completion realised as the specialisation at z of L(Π).
items.note: Proof: choose x ≠ z with G(K_x) split, a supercuspidal π′ of G(K_x) with L^{ss}(π′) irreducible (the local component at ∞ of the Kloosterman representation π(φ, χ) of Heinloth–Ngô–Yun), and a Poincaré series with Π_x ≅ π′, Π_z ≅ π and tame elsewhere ([GLo]).

items.name: Kloosterman sheaves and the irreducibility of their monodromy at ∞
items.statement: For the split almost-simple HNY setting and generic automorphic data, Kl_Ĝ(φ,χ) is the Hecke eigen local system of the constructed automorphic representation. HNY Theorem 2, under its good-prime restriction for nonsimply-laced types, states Swan∞(Ad Kl)=rank(Ĝ) and Lie(Ĝ)^{I∞}=0. items.name: Gan–Lomelí: globalisation of supercuspidals over function fields by Poincaré series
items.statement: (Gan–Lomelí, JEMS 20 (2018)) For supercuspidal representations π_i at finitely many places of a global function field, there is a cuspidal automorphic representation Π with these local components and tame (or unramified) components elsewhere, constructed as a constituent of a Poincaré series P_φ(g) = Σ_{γ∈G(K)} φ(γg) built from matrix coefficients supported on compact open subgroups; the series converges absolutely, and P_φ(1) ≠ 0 when the support meets G(K) only in the identity (or in a controlled finite group).

items.name: Corollary 4.3: tame local systems on G_m split into rank-one systems
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 4.2 with X = {0, ∞}, let V be a semisimple local system on Y = P^1 ∖ (X ∪ Z) whose local monodromy at 0 and ∞ is tame and whose semisimplified local monodromy at 0 or ∞ is abelian and Frobenius-semisimple. Then, after a finite extension of the coefficient field, V is a sum of rank-one local systems.

items.name: L. Lafforgue: decomposition of local systems into mixed ones up to constant twists

items.name: Kummer theory for K = k(t) and for k
items.statement: K′ is the compositum of the cyclic extensions of K of degree dividing q − 1 (the maximal abelian extension of exponent dividing q−1), and ψ : K^×/(K^×)^{q−1} ≅ X(K) = Hom_cont(Gal(K′/K), Q̄_ℓ^×) (4.4); C_T ⊂ K^×/(K^×)^{q−1} is generated by k^× and T, X_T = ψ(C_T); similarly ψ_k : k^× ≅ X(k) = Hom_cont(Gal(k′/k), Q̄_ℓ^×) (4.5) for the cyclic extension k′ of degree q − 1 (with q^{q−1} elements), with β^b := ψ_k(b)(β). items.name: Buildings, parahorics and Iwahori radicals for unramified groups
items.statement: For an unramified group G over K (quasi-split, split by an unramified extension, hence defined over k) with Borel B = TN, maximal k-split torus S ⊂ T, faithful representation ρ : G → Aut(V) with S-eigenbasis e_i of weights λ_i: at each place y, G(O_y) is hyperspecial; the preimage I_y of B(k_y) is an Iwahori subgroup with pro-p radical I(p) the preimage of N(k_y); the apartment A(A_y) ≅ X_*(A_y) ⊗ R with G(O_y) the stabiliser of 0, and for y ∈ P^1(k), A_y = S_y and the apartments are identified with X_*(S) ⊗ R. items.name: Lemma 5.1: the parahoric entry inequality
items.statement: Let F = k((t)), G an unramified semisimple group with maximal F-split torus S in a Borel B = TN, all defined over k; c a point of the apartment of S with parahoric G_c; ρ : G → Aut(V) faithful over k with S-eigenbasis e_1, …, e_n of weights λ_i. items.name: Lemma A.1 (Beuzart-Plessis): globalisation of discrete series up to cuspidal support
items.statement: Choose finite disjoint sets S,S′ and a compatible global central character ξ of Z⁰(A_K)/Z⁰(K). Let S, S′ ⊂ |X| be disjoint with S′ ∩ S_ram = ∅; for v ∈ S let π_v be a discrete series with central character ξ_v on Z^0(K_v), at least one π_{v_0} supercuspidal; for v ∈ S′ let X_v ⊂ (T̂_v//W_v)_{ξ_v} be a proper Zariski-closed subset. routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: tempered local parameters and the ramification of supercuspidal parameters
routes.brief: Import Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.5–7), Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4–6), Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.5), Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0–4), Arithmetic Galois representations (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2), and Reductive groups, Part II (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1–4). This candidate is held for revision. Its targets are the corrected item statements: unique essentially tempered refinement for discrete series, ramification of pure compactly induced supercuspidals for unramified non-tori over F_q((t)) with q>5, wild ramification under the precise small-subgroup condition, and the unramified principal-series conclusion under Levi compact-induction hypotheses. The GL_n ramification statements require n≥2 and the case-dependent residue bounds; the principal-series-after-base-change endpoint retains n=1. The no-incorrigibility statement excludes tori and quantifies hypotheses along the tower. Depth-zero purity and the p-adic consequences retain their comparison assumptions; Conjecture 11.7 and Questions 11.10–11.11 are open. Before design, close the intrinsic purity convention, matrix-bound proof, Weil-restriction character isolation, HNY/XZ and globalization suppliers. Extract each Poincaré-series, pseudo-coefficient, elliptic-orthogonality and close-fields carrier with its own API and proof dependencies; assess which reusable pieces belong to the shared owners rather than this consumer. Do not interpret the present route as permission to duplicate Kummer or finite-character infrastructure.
routes.reason: The paper's results are local theorems about Genestier–Lafforgue parameters proved by global arguments on shtuka parameters over k(P^1), in the direction of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands, which plans the global and local parametrisations themselves (GS.5, GS.7) but none of their temperedness or ramification properties. The nearest pending Part II, GlobalShtukasPartIIRamanujanArthur (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26), is about weight constraints on unramified components; this paper's ramification theorems, Poincaré-series globalisations, base change discussion and close-field conjecture go beyond it, and its one Ciubotaru–Harris input is routed there. The Poincaré-series and simple-trace-formula globalisations over function fields have no owner in the atlas and are only used here, so they are planned in this Part II.
routes.supersededBrief: Part II of Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands). It starts where that roadmap stops: GS.5 constructs V. Lafforgue's global semisimple parameters and GS.7 the Genestier–Lafforgue local parametrisation with its local–global comparison; this Part II proves local consequences for general reductive G. Source: Gan–Harris–Sawin–Beuzart-Plessis, 'Local parameters of supercuspidal representations' (Forum Math. Pi 12 (2024), e13; arXiv:2109.07737). Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 1.2: for G connected reductive over a local function field F and π an irreducible discrete series representation of G(F), there is a unique essentially tempered L-parameter L(π) whose semisimple parameter (1.1) is the Genestier–Lafforgue parameter L^{ss}(π); Corollary 1.3: a map L from essentially tempered representations to essentially tempered L-parameters refining Genestier–Lafforgue; Corollary 3.12: for G semisimple, Ad ∘ L(π) is pure of weight 0. Theorem 1.4: for F = k((t)), |k| = q > 5, G unramified and not a torus, and π ≅ c-Ind_U^{G(F)} τ supercuspidal with U compact open modulo centre, (i) if L^{ss}(π) is pure then L^{ss}(π) = L(π) is ramified (Theorem 7.1: f ∘ L^{ss}(π) is ramified, f : ^LG → ^LG/Z(Ĝ)); (ii) if U is sufficiently small (Definition 8.2), L^{ss}(π) is wildly ramified (Theorem 8.1). stageContracts.description:
### AA.4. Approximation and level maps

Prove weak approximation only in the cases justified by the relevant group theorem; keep failures for tori visible. Develop strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple groups outside S with the required noncompact local factor. Construct finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat levels, calculate degrees through stabilizer indices and prove Cartesian diagrams for Hecke correspondences. In non-neat cases retain quotient groupoids and stabilizers, using AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry for stack language.

targets.target: Weak approximation for algebraic groups, in the justified cases, with visible failure for tori
targets.note: Only field-level statements are proved: K is dense in every finite product of its completions (G_a), and a single element of Kˣ approximates targets at finitely many finite places while taking prescribed signs at the real places (the G_m form). Nothing for a general algebraic group, and no discussion of the failure of weak approximation for tori.

targets.target: Strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple G outside S with a noncompact local factor
targets.note: The one algebraic-group case is SL₂ over ℚ with S = {∞}, in congruence form: Tau Ceti proves SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/dℤ) surjective for every d, jointly at two coprime moduli, which is equivalent to density of SL₂(ℤ) in SL₂(ℤ̂). It is not stated adelically, and nothing covers other simply connected groups or other number fields; even additive strong approximation for a number field (density of K in the finite adeles) is unproved. Tau Ceti also proves strong approximation for the field of a function field. It has simply connected algebraic groups (Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SimplyConnected), but no approximation theorem uses them.

targets.target: Finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat levels, and degrees via stabilizer indices
targets.note: The abstract ingredients exist: for H ≤ G acting on E with E → E/G a quotient covering map, E/H → E/G is a covering map (`isCoveringMap_of_comp`), and the degree of a double coset H₁gH₂ is the index [H₁ : H₁ ∩ gH₂g⁻¹] (`degree_eq_relIndex`). No neatness predicate exists in either library — the word occurs only in three informal comments — and there are no adelic level quotients G(F)\G(𝔸)/K whose covering degrees could be computed.

targets.target: Cartesian diagrams for Hecke correspondences on adelic quotients
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a classical Hecke ring for GL_2 and GL_n double cosets (TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/), but no adelic double-coset correspondence with Cartesian squares of level covers.

targets.target: Quotient groupoids and stabilizers in the non-neat case
targets.note: No algebraic-stack quotient of an adelic double-coset space exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Proves existence of neat congruence subgroups and uses strong approximation in the same restricted form, so the neatness and approximation targets overlap.

stageContracts.description: ## R01.2. Decomposition groups, inertia and Weil–Deligne representations **Milestone:** `R01.2` Use a place or an embedding into a local separable closure to obtain restriction; prove invariance under changing that choice. Construct tame characters and fundamental characters of levels one and two. For ℓ different from the residue characteristic, prove quasi-unipotence and construct the monodromy operator and Weil–Deligne representation, including independence of the tame character. Distinguish the full object, its semisimplification, and its Frobenius semisimplification. With arithmetic Frobenius the relation is r(F)Nr(F)⁻¹=qN; do not copy a geometric-Frobenius formula unchanged. **Dependencies:** R01.1 (preceding layer).

targets.target: Restriction to a decomposition group through a place or an embedding into a local separable closure, with independence of the choice up to conjugacy
targets.note: Mathlib gives a continuous map of absolute Galois groups from a field embedding (for example K into its completion), explicitly depending on a chosen embedding of algebraic closures, and defines the decomposition and inertia subgroups of a valuation subring of an arbitrary extension L/K (no finiteness or Galois hypothesis). What is missing is the arithmetic content: a decomposition group attached to a place of a number field inside the absolute Galois group, and independence of the choice of place or embedding up to conjugacy. Tau Ceti's decomposition groups are for a finite extension of number fields or a place of a function field.

stageContracts.description: ## DWP.5. Weil II local weights and the analytic preparation **Milestone:** `DWP.5` Construct punctually ι-pure/ι-mixed lisse and constructible sheaves, their finite filtrations and weight classes modulo ℤ. Work with genuine finite coefficient fields/lattices before extending scalars; distinguish Weil descent from continuous Galois descent. Prove the coefficient-embedding and twist reductions used when weights are real. A formal real twist is not automatically a motivic Tate twist. Import LPV's inertia, nilpotent logarithm and monodromy-filtration carriers. Prove the local weight theorem for a punctually pure lisse sheaf on an open curve, including the weights of the monodromy graded pieces and the weights of boundary invariants of j_*F. Include quasi-unipotent reduction, finite covers, tensor and dual compatibility and the Frobenius–N relation. State the curve/equal- characteristic hypotheses; this is not the general mixed-characteristic weight–monodromy conjecture for varieties over a p-adic field. Construct Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate for ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings, then the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin positivity argument and the strict initial H¹ weight bound needed to start §3.2. Prove convergence, poles, multiplicities, tensor-power compatibility and the weight-integrality detection step. The boundary estimates and strict bound are proved here, not imported from DWP.7's desired result. **Dependencies:** DWP.0/DWP.2/DWP.4; EDC.1–2; LPV.0–2; PR196 sheaf L-functions. **Sources:** Weil II §§1.2–1.11/2.1–2.2, especially1.8.4 and2.2.10.

the trace formula for the actual stacks/quotients, stabilizer factors and a
globalization of prescribed local data. Track discriminant square roots and

unramified Hecke functions match. For cyclic base change use the separate
norm-map/unit-function and Hecke-transfer proof needed by ET.4; a general
twisted or weighted fundamental lemma is not smuggled into the ordinary theorem.

stageContracts.description: ## LPV.1. Inertia, variation and the monodromy operator Construct tame/wild inertia and the tame character t_ℓ:I→Z_ℓ(1) using the existing ramification and roots-of-unity APIs. Compare geometric actions on the nearby-cycle complex with the induced actions on cohomology. Construct the canonical/variation morphisms and prove their composition identities with T−1 in the chosen tame-generator convention, retaining Tate twists. For a proved unipotent action, define N through the finite logarithm and prove nilpotence, independence under change of a tame generator after interpreting N:V→V(-1), and exp(t_ℓ(σ)N)=ρ(σ). Prove the quasi-unipotence theorem in the geometric coefficient setting actually used, with finite-extension reduction, wild inertia and continuity checked. An arbitrary continuous representation over an algebraically closed residue field is not declared quasi-unipotent. This is the geometric supplier, while ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations owns the general Weil–Deligne carrier and conductor of an arithmetic representation. Construct the uniquely characterized monodromy filtration centered at a specified integer: N lowers the filtration by two and N^r identifies opposite graded pieces with the appropriate twist. Prove this linear algebra and its functorial properties independently of any claim that these pieces have the corresponding Frobenius weights. Sources: SGA 7 I I/VI for geometric monodromy, SGA 7 II XIII, and the linear-algebra conventions in Deligne II §§1.6–1.7. ### RG2.1. Relative roots and valued root data

Construct relative roots from a maximal E-split torus, relative Weyl group, root subgroups and filtrations indexed by their actual valuation sets. Include multipliable roots and nonsplit root groups. Establish commutator estimates, conjugation by the torus and compatibility under unramified extension. Build the affine root system and apartment from the valued datum. ### RG2.2. Buildings and group action

Glue apartments by the Bruhat–Tits equivalence relation; prove well-defined affine transition maps, the building axioms, the G(E)-action, apartment existence for pairs of points and the relation between reduced and enlarged buildings. Prove independence of auxiliary root parametrizations. Develop facets, closure order, fixers, compactness modulo center and the fixed-point statement for bounded subgroups with its hypotheses. Construct the GL_n model from homothety classes of norms/lattice chains and identify the SL_2 tree as a validation example.

### RG2.3. Parahoric and congruence group schemes

For a facet construct the smooth affine O_E-group scheme with connected special fiber and the prescribed root-group charts. Prove its characterization by integral points, generic fiber G, connected reductive quotient of the special fiber, pro-unipotent radical and reduction map. Identify pro-p congruence subgroups and prove their compact openness. Prove compatibility for nested facets and unramified base change; record the distinctions between connected parahorics, fixer group schemes and hyperspecial models.

stageContracts.description:
### RG2.4. Decompositions and double cosets

Prove Iwasawa decomposition using an appropriate special maximal compact subgroup. Prove the Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions in their exact generality, with the correct relative cocharacter lattice, dominance conditions and stabilizers. Derive finiteness of compact-open double coset decompositions and index formulas. Supply rank-one and nonsplit examples showing why the split simply connected formula cannot be used universally.

stageContracts.description:
### SR.2. Induction, compact induction and Jacquet functors

Construct smooth induction from closed subgroups and compact induction with support compact modulo the subgroup. Prove Frobenius reciprocity with correct adjoint direction and hypotheses, induction in stages and Mackey filtrations. For P=MN define unnormalized induction and N-coinvariants, then normalized induction/Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character. Prove exactness in the valid coefficient regime, compatibility with duals for admissible representations, and the geometric lemma with double-coset indexing. A characteristic-p analogue of an ℓ≠p exactness theorem is not an automatic target.

stageContracts.description:
### SR.3. Admissible complex representations

Prove finite-dimensionality of compact-open invariants for irreducible smooth complex representations of reductive G(E), finite length of parabolic induction of finite-length admissibles, smooth contragredient duality, matrix-coefficient criteria for supercuspidality and temperedness, and the subquotient description by supercuspidal support. Construct the Bernstein decomposition and Bernstein center as natural endomorphisms of the identity, with its action on every object. Prove invariance under inner isomorphisms and compatibility with products. Classification is not assumed to prove basic admissibility.

### SR.4. Spherical representations and Satake

For unramified G and a hyperspecial subgroup K, construct the Satake transform and prove the isomorphism with the appropriate invariant algebra on the dual torus, retaining the relative Weyl group and Frobenius action. Specify coefficients and q-half normalization; record the integral unnormalized form separately. Identify Hecke eigencharacters with unramified semisimple parameters. Verify split tori and GL_n explicitly and provide the normalization dictionary consumed by IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants. Classical Satake and geometric Satake are separate constructions with a comparison obligation.
